english.title: Possess intoxicants on a train service - railway bye-law
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), possessed intoxicating liquor

(A)_[in a train,]_
(B)_[while attempting to enter a train,]_

the possession of which on the train had been prohibited by notice
english.legislation: Contrary to byelaws 4(2) and 24 of the Railway Byelaws.

english.notes:
(i) Byelaw 24(2) provides a power for authorised person to remove persons from the railway. See Byelaw 23(1) for the associated power to require a name and address.
(ii) Schedule 2 to the Railway Byelaws provides that in byelaw 25(1) the following operators are excluded from the definition of operator; Great Central Railway (Nottingham) Limited, London Underground Limited Tube Lines Limited and Tyne and Wear Passenger Transport Executive.
(iii) This offence applies from the 26th December 2025 due to changes made by the Railway Byelaws Amendment Order 2025. For the offence applying before this date, see H8044.
(iv) The Railway Byelaws 2005 were made by the Strategic Rail Authority under section 219 of the Transport Act 2000 and confirmed under Schedule 20 to the Transport Act 2000, both of which were repealed on 15th October 2015. Section 46(4) of the Railways Act 2005 provides that these Byelaws remain in force.
